text: - `--key <FIELD>` — **required**. Payload key to facet on (e.g. `city`).
- `--limit <N>` — max facet hits to return. Default `10`.
- `--exact` — count each value exactly (slower). Approximate is the default.
- Filter flags as below.
Prints one JSON line per hit: `{"value": ..., "count": N}`.
### Filtering and output (every subcommand)

- `--filter <JSON>` — an arbitrary payload filter in Qdrant's filter DSL (the `filter` field of a REST request). Curl `--data` style: a literal JSON string, `@path` to read from a file, or `@-` to read from stdin. Any condition the DSL can express works here, so there are no per-condition flags.

- `--filter-key` / `--filter-value` — shortcut for the common "field equals value" case. Must be given together, and are mutually exclusive with `--filter`. The value is parsed as an integer or boolean when it looks like one, otherwise as a string.
- `--limit <N>` — max points (or facet hits) to return. Default `10`. Scroll / search / text / facet only.
- `--with-vectors` — include vectors in the output. Scroll / search / text only.
## Running it
Scroll and search results print as one JSON object per line (`id`, `payload`, `vector`, plus `score` and `version` for searches).
## Live reload — watching a leader's writes
Both flags keep the tool running after the first answer. Each iteration live_reloads the shard from the backend, re-runs the **same** request, and prints a diff against the previous results:

```
+ {...}   point appeared
- {...}   point disappeared
~ {old} -> {new}   same id, changed content
```

A pure reordering of unchanged rows prints nothing (`no changes`). This is the fastest way to watch a leader writing into the same bucket, and to catch staleness or consistency bugs in the follower read path.
- `--live-reload <SECONDS>` — live_reload on a timer (minimum 1).

- `--live-reload-key` — live_reload when you press Enter instead. Better when stepping through a debugger on the leader. Not compatible with `@-` (stdin) request arguments, since it reads stdin itself.
The two are mutually exclusive. A failed live_reload is logged and retried on the next trigger — the shard keeps serving its previous state rather than dying.

```sh
cargo run -p edge-shard-query -- <CONNECTION FLAGS> <SUBCOMMAND> <SUBCOMMAND FLAGS>
```
## Examples
Scroll with a JSON filter, against a local MinIO/RustFS:

```sh
cargo run -p edge-shard-query -- \
    --backend  aws \
    --endpoint http://localhost:9000 \
    --bucket   test-bucket \
    --region   us-east-1 \
    --access-key rustfsadmin \
    --secret-key rustfsadmin \
    --prefix   collection/0 \
    --uio-trace trace.jsonl \
    scroll \
    --filter '{"must":[{"key":"city","match":{"value":"London"}}]}' \
    --limit  20
```

Dense search on GCS, query vector from a file:

```sh
cargo run -p edge-shard-query -- \
    --backend gcs \
    --bucket  my-bucket \
    --gcs-service-account-path /path/to/key.json \
    --prefix  collection/0 \
    search \
    --vector @query.json \
    --limit  5
```

Sparse search (note `--using`, since sparse vectors are named):

```sh
cargo run -p edge-shard-query -- \
    --backend  aws \
    --endpoint http://localhost:9000 \
    --bucket   test-bucket \
    --prefix   collection/0 \
    search-sparse \
    --using  text \
    --vector '{"indices": [12, 700, 5301], "values": [0.4, 0.9, 0.2]}' \
    --limit  5
```

Connection flags must come **before** the subcommand; request flags come after it. For repeated use, build once (`cargo build -p edge-shard-query --release`) and call `target/release/edge-shard-query` directly.

BM25 text search, statistics gathered over one city only:

```sh
cargo run -p edge-shard-query -- \
    --backend  aws \
    --endpoint http://localhost:9000 \
    --bucket   test-bucket \
    --prefix   collection/0 \
    text \
    --field body \
    --query "amber harbor" \
    --idf-corpus '{"must":[{"key":"city","match":{"value":"harbor"}}]}' \
    --limit 5
```

## Choosing a backend

Read straight from a running Qdrant peer — no object storage at all:

```sh
cargo run -p edge-shard-query -- \
    --backend    uio-grpc \
    --endpoint   http://localhost:6334 \
    --collection my_collection \
    --shard-id   0 \
    scroll \
    --limit 10
```

Watch a leader's writes propagate, re-running a filtered search every 2 seconds:

```sh
cargo run -p edge-shard-query -- \
    --backend  aws \
    --endpoint http://localhost:9000 \
    --bucket   test-bucket \
    --prefix   collection/0 \
    --live-reload 2 \
    search \
    --filter-key city --filter-value London \
    --limit 20
```
`--backend` selects where segments are read from. It defaults to `aws`.
## Troubleshooting

- **Nothing found / shard opens with 0 segments.** Check `--prefix` actually points at the shard root (the level holding `segments/`), and that the leader wrote a segment manifest. For `uio-grpc`, the peer needs `QDRANT__FEATURE_FLAGS__WRITE_SEGMENT_MANIFEST=true`.
- **Stale results.** The disk cache persists across runs by default. Delete `--cache-dir` (or the default temp subdirectory) to force a cold fetch.
- **`--vector` rejected on `search-sparse`.** Sparse takes `{"indices": [...], "values": [...]}` or `12:0.4,700:0.9` — not a plain float array.
- **Vector name not in shard config.** `--using` must name a vector that exists in the shard; with no `--using`, the default/unnamed vector must exist.
- **Credentials.** `--access-key` and `--secret-key` must be supplied together, or both omitted to fall back to the AWS default credential chain.

| Backend | What it reads | Shard addressed by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `aws` | AWS S3 or any S3-compatible store (MinIO, RustFS, LocalStack) | `--bucket` + `--prefix` |
| `gcs` | Google Cloud Storage | `--bucket` + `--prefix` |
| `uio-grpc` | A running Qdrant peer's `StorageRead` gRPC service | `--collection` + `--shard-id` |
### `--prefix` (object storage only)

The key prefix inside the bucket that points at the **edge-shard root** — the directory containing `edge_config.json` and `segments/`. Empty means the bucket root. A shard for collection `foo`, shard `0` typically lives at `foo/0`.

An `edge_config.json` is *not* required: segments are discovered from the leader's segment manifest, and the shard config is derived from the segments themselves. Leave `--prefix` empty for `uio-grpc`, which addresses the shard by collection and shard id instead.
### Connection flags
All of these accept an environment variable as a fallback, shown in brackets.

**AWS / S3-compatible**
- `--bucket` [`BLOB_BUCKET`] — bucket name, no scheme prefix. Required.
- `--endpoint` [`S3_ENDPOINT`] — custom S3 endpoint. Set for MinIO/RustFS/LocalStack; **omit for real AWS**.
- `--region` [`S3_REGION`] — e.g. `us-east-1`. Required for real AWS, optional for S3-compatible endpoints.
- `--access-key` [`S3_ACCESS_KEY`] / `--secret-key` [`S3_SECRET_KEY`] — must be given **together**. If both are omitted, the AWS default credential chain is used.
- `--session-token` [`S3_SESSION_TOKEN`] — for short-lived credentials.
- `--s3-express` [`S3_EXPRESS`] — for S3 Express One Zone directory buckets (named `*--x-s3`).
**GCS**
- `--bucket` [`BLOB_BUCKET`] — required.
- `--gcs-service-account-path` [`GCS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH`] — path to a service-account JSON key file.

- `--gcs-service-account-key` [`GCS_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY`] — the key contents inline. The *path* form takes precedence if both are set; if neither is set, application default credentials (ADC) are used.
**uio-grpc**
- `--endpoint` — the peer's public gRPC URL, e.g. `http://localhost:6334`. Required.
- `--collection` [`QDRANT_COLLECTION`] — required.
- `--shard-id` — defaults to `0`.
- `--api-key` [`QDRANT_API_KEY`] — omit for an unauthenticated peer.
> The peer must run with `QDRANT__FEATURE_FLAGS__WRITE_SEGMENT_MANIFEST=true`, otherwise the shard has no segment manifest and discovery fails.
### Tuning flags (all backends)

- `--cache-dir` — local mirror directory for the segment disk cache. Each remote block is fetched once and served locally afterwards. Defaults to a stable subdirectory of the system temp dir, so **the cache persists across runs** — delete it to force a cold read.
- `--search-threads` — size of the shard's search thread pool (used to read segments in parallel at open, and to run searches). `0` derives it from the CPU count.

- `--no-load-profile` — by default the shard is opened *for the specific request*, warming only the segment components that request will touch and leaving the rest cold. This flag disables that and warms everything per the persisted segment configs, like a long-lived deployment would. Use it when benchmarking steady-state behaviour rather than cold start.

- `--deferred-threshold-kb <KB>` — hide points the leader defers under `prevent_unoptimized`: points of appendable segments past this threshold, in KB like the indexing threshold (pass the leader's indexing threshold, capped by an explicit max segment size). Without it every stored point is visible. Conflicts with `--no-load-profile`.

- `--uio-trace <PATH>` — record every network storage request into this file, one JSON line each.
  Open the file with `tools/uio-trace-visualizer.html` to see the read timeline.
# edge-shard-query
## Subcommands
### `scroll` — paginate over points
- `--offset <ID>` — start id, to resume a previous page. Accepts an integer or a UUID string.
- `--order-by <FIELD>` — order by a payload field instead of by id.
Prints the records plus a `next_page_offset` line to feed back into `--offset`.
### `search` — dense nearest-neighbour search

- `--vector` — the query vector. Accepts a JSON array (`[0.1, 0.2, ...]`), a comma-separated list (`0.1,0.2,...`), or `@path` / `@-` to read either form from a file or stdin. **If omitted, a random vector is used**, with its dimension read from the shard config once the shard is open — handy for a quick smoke test.
- `--using <NAME>` — which named vector to search. Omit for the default/unnamed vector.
- `--offset <N>` — results to skip before collecting `--limit`. Default `0`.
- `--score-threshold <F>` — only return results scoring at least this.
- `--hnsw-ef <N>` — HNSW beam width. Larger is more accurate and slower.
- `--exact` — search exhaustively, bypassing HNSW. Slow but exact; useful to check recall.

An experimental binary that opens a `ReadOnlyEdgeShard` **directly over object storage** (S3/S3-compatible or GCS) — or over a running Qdrant peer's `StorageRead` gRPC service — and runs a single read request against it.
### `search-sparse` — sparse nearest-neighbour search

- `--vector` — **required**. Accepts a JSON object (`{"indices": [12, 700], "values": [0.4, 0.9]}`), a comma-separated list of `index:value` pairs (`12:0.4,700:0.9`), or `@path` / `@-`. Indices need not be sorted.
- `--using <NAME>` — sparse vectors are named, so this is **usually required**. Omit only if the shard stores its sparse vector under the default (empty) name.
- `--offset`, `--score-threshold`, `--exact` — as for `search` (`--exact` bypasses the sparse index).
### `text`: BM25 search over a text index

- `--field <FIELD>`: **required**. Payload field to score. Its text index must have `scoring` set (`edge-tool create --payload-index body:bm25` builds one, `edge-tool load-beir` fills it with a BEIR corpus).
- `--query <TEXT>`: **required**, non-empty. Tokenized as the field's index tokenizes a query. Taken literally, so it may start with `@`.
With several masters (up to 5, e.g. one per career track), `list_resumes` shows them; tailor from the one that fits the job, or the default.
## 3. Tailor (per job)
Job descriptions come pasted in chat, or as `.md`/`.txt` files in `jobs/` (ignore `jobs/README.md` and the `jobs/done/` and `jobs/.work/` folders). For each job:

1. **Add the job.** Read it and extract the keywords, then:
   `add_job job_description=@/abs/path/jobs/acme.md company="Acme" role="Platform Engineer" keywords:=@/abs/path/jobs/.work/acme-keywords.json`
   The keywords object has `required_skills`, `preferred_skills`, `experience_requirements`, `education_requirements`, `key_responsibilities` and `keywords` (lists of short strings); company and role go in the `company` and `role` arguments. A job pasted in chat is saved to `jobs/.work/<company>.md` first (scratch, not the batch); files the user saved in `jobs/` are the batch.
2. **Read the source.** `get_resume resume_id=<master id>`. Start from its `resume_data` exactly as returned, including `sectionMeta` and `customSections`; a copy from anywhere else fails validation.
3. **Write the tailored version** by the rules below.

4. **Save and check:** `tailor_and_verify @/abs/path/jobs/.work/acme-tailor.json` with `{"source_resume_id", "job_id", "resume_data", "title": "<Role> @ <Company>"}`. It validates, saves a new resume (the master is untouched), renders the PDF, parse-checks it, scores it and adds an Applied card to the tracker. Call it **once per job**: every successful call adds another resume and tracker card, so fix things afterwards with `update_resume`.

- The result is long. The fields you need: `saved`, `resume.resume_id`, `score.overall_score`, `score.missing_keywords`, `page_count` and `issues` (`verify_resume` returns the same `score`, `page_count` and `issues`).
- `saved: false`: nothing was written. Read `validation.violations`, fix them (or adopt `validation.repaired_resume_data`) and call it again.
- `validation.grounding_warnings` are advisory: check each one against the source and fix anything unsupported.
5. **Fix `issues`**, then re-check with `verify_resume resume_id=<id>`. Stop after two or three rounds and tell the user what is left.

| Issue | What to do |
   |---|---|
   | `injectable_keywords` | Work those keywords into existing bullets or the skills list; the master supports them |
   | `over_page_limit` | Tighten the summary and bullets; do not drop roles |
   | `multi_column`, `low_order_fidelity` | Suggest a single-column template such as `swiss-single` |
   | `garbled_glyphs`, `fields_missing` | Check unusual characters and empty fields |
   | `no_job_keywords` | The job was added without keywords, so there is no score: extract them, call `set_job_keywords`, then `verify_resume` |
   | `weak_writing` | A line has an em dash or a weak opener: `writing.findings` gives each path. Fix it in the writing rounds below |
   | `render_failed` | The web app is not running at the URL in `render_error`: start it |
Work in this order: **set up** (once), **master resume** (once), **tailor** (per job), **hand off** to the UI. Skip a step that is already done. Talk to the user in their language.
Edit with `update_resume resume_id=<id> resume_data:=@…` (it replaces the whole resume, so start from `get_resume`), then `recalculate_ats_score resume_id=<id>`.

6. **Run two writing rounds.** The app's own tailoring critiques and rewrites once; you have no API cost, so do it twice. Each round:
   1. Critique the summary and every bullet against the writing rubric below, together with the `writing.findings` that `verify_resume` returned.
   2. Rewrite only the lines that break the rubric. Every number, name, tool and skill of the original line stays; add none. A line with no number gets its outcome or scope from what the line already says; if a real number would help, ask the user instead of guessing.
   3. `update_resume`, then `verify_resume`. `writing.score` should rise and `weak_writing` should clear.
7. **Batch from `jobs/`:** after each job, move its file to `jobs/done/` so a rerun skips it.
### Writing rubric
The app's critique prompt uses this exact text (a test keeps the two in sync).
<!-- writing-rubric:start -->
## The command

- Start every bullet with a strong action verb in the past tense (present tense for a current role). Never open with "Responsible for", "Helped with", "Assisted in", "Involved in", "Participated in", "Worked on" or "Tasked with".
- Shape each bullet as Challenge, Action, Result: the situation, what the candidate did, and what changed because of it.

- State the result. Keep every number in the source exactly. Never invent a number, percentage, amount, count or time saved, and never add size words ("significantly", "dramatically", "greatly") the source does not use.
- When the source has no number, state the result through scope and outcome the source already gives: who used the work, what it replaced, what it made possible, how often it ran.
- Keep every fact: each number, name, product, tool, skill and outcome in the original stays in the rewrite. Add none.
- One idea per bullet, at most about 35 words. No first-person pronouns ("I", "my").
- No em dashes ("—") or double hyphens ("--"). Use a comma, a semicolon or a new sentence.

- Avoid stock phrases such as "spearheaded", "leveraged", "orchestrated", "utilized", "synergy", "cutting-edge" and "results-driven".
<!-- writing-rubric:end -->
### Tailoring rules
These are the rules the app's own tailoring follows, and the validator enforces most of them.
- Keep `personalInfo`, employers, job titles, locations, dates (`years`, copied exactly, months included), the number of entries and the number of bullets.
- Never add a skill, tool, technology, certification, employer, metric or responsibility the source does not contain. Never raise seniority.
- Rephrase existing bullets to use the job's wording where the source already shows that experience. Reorder skills by relevance, but never remove one.
- Rewrite the summary for the role from facts already in the resume.
- Write in the resume's language. No em dashes. Avoid stock phrases such as "spearheaded", "leveraged", "orchestrated", "utilized", "synergy", "cutting-edge" and "results-driven".

- If the job needs something the user has not shown, say so; do not paper over it. `score.missing_keywords` lists what the resume does not support: report those to the user as gaps they can add in the editor if they really have them. A low score from honest gaps is the right result.

From the repository root:

```bash
uv run --directory apps/backend resume-matcher <tool> [arguments]
```

- The `date_consistency` part of the score is low when the source mixes date formats (`Mar 2022 - Present` beside `2015 - 2019`). Keep the dates as written and tell the user they can make the formats match in their master resume.
## 4. Hand off to the UI

When done, give the user a short table: role and company, ATS score (`score.overall_score`), pages, remaining issues and gaps, and the link `http://localhost:3000/builder?id=<resume_id>`. Then tell them:
- The dashboard lists every resume: <http://localhost:3000/dashboard>. Open pages update on their own within a few seconds of each save, so there is no need to reload.
- In the editor they can change any text, section order, template and formatting. Changes save automatically, and **Download** exports the PDF.
- The application tracker is at <http://localhost:3000/tracker>.
- The app's AI buttons show a prompt to paste back to you.
- If they are editing a resume while you save it, the editor asks them whether to keep their edits or take yours. Prefer to work on resumes they are not editing.

## Boundaries
- No tool deletes anything. `update_resume`, `set_*`, `set_job_keywords` and `update_application` overwrite what they target: read it first.
- Change the app's settings only to switch on agent mode, and only after the user agrees.
- The user's resume, job descriptions and exports stay out of git: `jobs/` and `apps/backend/data/` are gitignored. Never commit them.
- Prefer MCP? The same tools run as an MCP server (`resume-matcher-mcp`); see [SETUP.md](../../../SETUP.md#use-resume-matcher-from-claude-code-or-claude-desktop-mcp).
